punchline: Fighter pilot John Boyd told young officers they would reach a fork where they could be somebody or do something.
thirty_sec: In 1973 Air Force strategist John Boyd called in a promising young officer and laid out two roads. On one you become somebody, with promotions and a seat in the club, at the cost of compromises. On the other you do something, and you may never be promoted but you keep your integrity. Boyd chose the second and never rose above colonel. Ryan Holiday says ego blurs this choice.
